service.name: Wedding ceremony music
service.serviceType: Acoustic and Spanish guitar for wedding ceremonies
service.description: An acoustic or Spanish guitarist for a wedding ceremony prelude, processional and recessional, with an announcement microphone for the officiant, across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.a: For the prelude and the processional, yes. A lyric pulls attention to the words at the moment everyone is watching the aisle. An interlude is where a sung song works, because the guests are seated and still and there's nothing else to look at. Signet Artists books ceremony musicians across Denver and the Colorado mountains.

Yes. Outdoors an unamplified officiant is lost past about the fourth row, so an announcement microphone comes with every size, and the officiant, the readings and the vows carry through the same small system as the guitar.

faqs.q: Can you play an outdoor ceremony?
faqs.a: Yes, and most ceremonies here are outside. It takes a covered, level and dry spot for the musician, power run to it, and a move-indoors call written before the day. Open air has no walls to send the sound back, so the small system carries the same gentle level to the back rows, and the spot is chosen with the wind in mind, because wind puts noise straight into the officiant's microphone. Colorado evenings cool fast after sunset, so a late-afternoon mountain ceremony gets the weather call written into the contract.

faqs.q: How much space does a guitarist need?
faqs.a: A spot of about 6 by 4 feet beside the aisle, level and out of the sun, with power if the small system is used.

faqs.q: How much to tip ceremony musicians?
faqs.a: Nothing is expected. The figure agreed for your date is the whole cost of the music, so a gratuity is a personal choice. If you'd like to do something, credit the musicians by name to your photographer before the gallery goes out.
